hints: Focus on which functional groups are acidic enough to react with dilute aqueous NaOH, carboxylic acids or alcohols?
Remember that excess $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduces each $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ group to a primary alcohol $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, so work out what functional groups are left in J.
Compare tartaric acid and J side by side and ask yourself which one still contains an acidic group that NaOH can neutralise.
walkthrough:
**Spot the functional groups in tartaric acid**

Tartaric acid is $\text{HO}_2\text{CCH(OH)CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$. It has two carboxylic acid groups, $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, and two alcohol groups, $-\text{OH}$.

Carboxylic acids are acidic enough to be neutralised by $\text{NaOH(aq)}$. Alcohols are not.

**Find the structure of J after reduction**

$\text{LiAlH}_4$ is a strong reducing agent. With excess, it reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols:
$$-\text{CO}_2\text{H} \xrightarrow{\text{excess LiAlH}_4} -\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
So both ends are reduced:
$$\text{HO}_2\text{CCH(OH)CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H} \rightarrow \text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$$
Product J is a tetra-ol containing only alcohol $-\text{OH}$ groups and no $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ groups.

**Test each with NaOH(aq)**

Tartaric acid reacts as an acid-base neutralisation to form a salt and water:
$$\text{RCO}_2\text{H} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2\text{Na} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
J contains only alcohol groups, which do not react with dilute $\text{NaOH(aq)}$. Therefore only tartaric acid reacts.

options.A: Incorrect. While tartaric acid does react, J does not. This choice assumes alcohol $-\text{OH}$ groups react with $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ like acids do, but alcohols are far too weakly acidic for this.
options.B: Correct. Tartaric acid contains two $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ groups which are neutralised by $\text{NaOH(aq)}$. J is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$, which contains only alcohol groups that do not react with $\text{NaOH(aq)}$.
options.C: Incorrect and backwards. It suggests the tetra-ol J reacts but the dicarboxylic acid does not. Carboxylic acids readily react with NaOH, alcohols do not.
options.D: Incorrect. It misses that carboxylic acids are neutralised by NaOH. Tartaric acid definitely reacts to give the sodium salt plus water, even though J does not.
